_comment_format: THIS FILE IS STRICT JSON, NOT JSONC. Do not add `//` comments.
Measured 2026-08-23 (T242): 27 of its ~32 readers parse it with a plain
`json.loads` — only a handful go through `strip_jsonc`. Adding one comment line
broke `tasks-bounds` immediately and would have broken 26 more gates, each with a
JSONDecodeError naming a line number rather than the cause. The estate's config
preference is JSONC, and this file is the exception because its reader set is wide
and unversioned. Document values with `_comment` / `_comment_<key>` arrays instead,

naming._comment: T119 AC4 — decided 2026-07-22. Change dirs keep the YYYY-MM-DD- prefix: it gives chronology and backtracing at a glance, which is worth more than CLI ergonomics. The cost is that openspec CLI >=1.6.0 REJECTS names starting with a digit, so: create letter-first, then rename the directory. Use POSITIONAL commands (`openspec validate <name> --type change`) — the `--change <name>` FLAG rejects dated names. `openspec list` and `validate --all` work either way.

_comment_gh_account: The ACTING PRINCIPAL — the account `gh auth switch --user` pins, isolated via GH_CONFIG_DIR.
NOT the board owner. `sync_github.py` used to read `OWNER = ACCOUNT`, collapsing the two
into one string; see `board` below for why one value cannot serve both (T242).

_comment: The Projects v2 board, declared ONCE (T242). Before this block, one board had THREE
resolution strategies and no declared identity: `sync_github.py` looked it up by
(owner, title) and took the FIRST match, while `populate_project_fields.py` and
`sync_project_fields.py` each hardcoded (owner, number) — and both also hardcoded the
owner TYPE into their GraphQL root as `user(login:...)`, which an organization-owned
project is simply not reachable through.
Every one of those failure modes EXITS 0. A stale owner finds a real, live-looking board
(a `gh project copy` leaves two boards with the same title), items land on it, and nothing
reaches the intended one.
`number` is authoritative and `title` is the GUARD: resolution is by number, then the title
is CHECKED against this declaration. Title-matching alone is what the copy defeats.
`owner_type` decides the GraphQL root (`user` vs `organization`) and must change in the
same edit as `owner`. Changing one without the other resolves to null, not to an error —
there is no way to tell a user from an organization by login.
Read it through `project/scripts/board_identity.py`. Held by `just board-identity-test`.

secrets._comment: T119 AC2b (DONE — verified 2026-07-25): secrets reach a command by PROCESS INJECTION via `run` — never a file. wom7web/.env, the apps/*/.dev.vars exports, `dotenv-load` and every `infisical export` call are GONE, and debt row D18 was deleted with them. state_surface._comment: T145 — STATE.md is the handoff surface, and it is now MECHANICALLY maintained instead of by convention. Owner directive 2026-07-26: regenerate the top-10 hot header whenever a ticket closes through the SDLC, and refresh it when one advances a stage. The generated managed block holds the top-10 hot table + per-repo dirty/unpushed/HEAD + gate exit codes + the rowless-ticket set; prose OUTSIDE the markers is editorial and never touched by the tool.
state_surface._gate: `state-check` is wired at pre-push and BLOCKS. It is verify-only — it never rewrites the file, because a hook that mutates a tracked file mid-commit must re-stage it and can fight the commit. On failure: run `just state-save`, then review the editorial sections by hand.
state_surface._why_hot_is_generated: The top-10 hot ranking used to be re-derived from prose by whichever agent was in the chair, then hand-written — so it reflected that agent and went stale the moment a ticket moved (a recorded entry still claimed '29 fileless tickets' after they were fixed). It is now computed by `just tasks hot` from recorded fields with the score components printed, and `state-check` compares the ranked ORDER, so closing or advancing a ticket makes the header provably stale rather than quietly wrong.

retention._comment: T174 (§0q deliverable 3, asked 2026-07-25, unbuilt until 2026-08-07) — T145 made the MECHANICAL block generated and deliberately never touched the prose, which is where the growth was: measured 2026-08-07 the file was 333,768 B / 4,141 lines and 93.9% of it was dated history, having gone 5 KB → 333 KB in 16 days. `w0m-state-load` tells the next agent to read it, so orientation cost ~83k tokens before any work started. Retention is declared HERE rather than living in state_doctor.py so the policy is readable without reading the implementation — the 2026-08-07 Obsidian-port incident is what that rule is for: a governance file that had INFERRED a fact disagreed with reality for twelve days.
retention._budget_rationale: MEASURED, then RAISED. The estimate was ~31,000 B; the actual post-rotation file is 47,246 B / 450 lines — the ⭐ block (8.7 KB), the consolidated §4 gotchas and the 56-row archive index are all bigger than projected. At the first-chosen 65,536 that left only 28% headroom, i.e. ONE session of slack, so the budget was raised to 80 KiB / 900 lines (~42% headroom, 2-3 sessions). Per T135 AC8 a gate set close to the post-change size starts effectively red and gets bypassed — and `--no-verify` is prohibited here, so 'always red' is not a survivable design. Steady state is flat, not growing: each session adds a pickup block (~9 KB) and `state-save` rotates the previous one out; the only monotonic growth is one ~200 B archive-index row per session, which reaches this budget in ~150 sessions. ⚠️ Do NOT raise it again to accommodate a file that stopped rotating — check `just state-rotate` ran first.
retention._why_two_patterns: These two literal shapes covered 19 of 66 sections and 188,319 B — 56.4% of the file — and identifying them needs NO judgement, which is what makes rotation separable from the triage of the remaining 37. Add a pattern only when a new shape is provably mechanical; anything requiring a reading is a triage decision and belongs in the disposition record.
never_rotate: ^## 4\. Gotchas the next agent MUST know
retention._verbatim: Rotation MOVES content and must never transform it. This is a security clause, not a style one: several sections are the only record of credential incidents (the 2026-07-12 leak, the force-push-resurrects-leaked-objects warning), and a tool that 'helpfully' rewrote one would be an unreviewed edit to a security record.
retention._disposition: Every editorial section must appear exactly once with a disposition — archived | promoted-to-auto-memory | promoted-to-CLAUDE.md | kept-live. An unaccounted section is a HARD FAILURE, never a default-archive: the failure to fear in this change is not a slow triage but a lesson quietly dropped with nobody able to tell.

second_surface._comment: T174 AC5 — the reason the naive fix is wrong. MEMORY.md is auto-loaded EVERY session; STATE.md is read ONCE, and only when an agent chooses to. Draining one into the other converts a large occasional cost into a permanent one, so `archived` is the DEFAULT disposition and promotion must earn its place. If the COMBINED cost of both surfaces rises, the split is wrong.
second_surface._unversioned: 🔴 This path is outside git, per-machine, and invisible to every gate — a THIRD occupant of the D32/D15 class and worse than the other two, being per-USER rather than per-workspace. Tracked as D36. No secret, token or connection string may be promoted there, and every promoted fact must leave a versioned pointer in the repo so a fact leaving git still produces a reviewable diff.

lessons_surface._comment: T232 AC11 — LESSONS.md is the earned rules register. Retention limits prevent unbounded context growth, while `just lessons` provides active querying.

retention._budget_rationale: Measured 2026-09-15: 711 lines / 63,311 bytes across 7 theme sections. Bound declared at 1,000 lines / 90 KiB provides headroom while ensuring agents can search and orient without context bloat.

layers._comment: The two-layer layout, and why the split matters: integrity is computed over the GOVERNED layer, agents read the RUNTIME layer. Read by project/scripts/ide_trace.py (`just ide-trace` / `--enforce`); the per-tool autoload knowledge and the non-negotiables checked for parity live in the policy file, never here. ⚠️ `connected` is a DICT here because w0m is one project spanning seven repos under this single sdlc.json — keys are `repos` keys, and each repo is scanned as its own unit since each autoloads its own CLAUDE.md. mcp._comment: T130: the MCP servers enabled for this project — the top rung of the tool ladder (MCP > CLI > python > ts > bash). Names + purpose ONLY: configuration and credentials live in the host Claude config (~/.claude.json) or plugins, NEVER here. `enabled` = intended project surface; `scope` = where it is configured (global = ~/.claude.json, plugin = a Claude Code plugin, session = host/plugin-provided, availability varies). Live availability is a harness fact, not a file fact — do not assume a server is connected because it is listed here (e.g. supabase is often NOT connected → psql fallback). T154 AC8: every entry MUST record `transport` (stdio | remote | local-http). `local-http` additionally requires `bind` + `auth` — it is the only kind a local port scan can reconcile against, and the only kind that can be the finding this ticket started from. `just mcp-exposure` fails on an entry with no transport.

obsidian-wom7web.auth: required — per-vault semantic-vault-mcp apiKey; unauthenticated probe returns 401
obsidian-wom7web.purpose: Obsidian vault access over MCP, served by the **`semantic-vault-mcp`** plugin ("Semantic Notes Vault MCP" 0.11.42, Aaron Bockelie) running inside an Obsidian renderer process — NOT a standalone daemon, so it exists only while that vault window is open. 🔴 CORRECTED 2026-08-07: this entry previously attributed both ports to `obsidian-local-rest-api` v5.0.2. That was wrong, and the estate contradicted itself about it — `project/mcp-exposure-baseline.json` had already named the right plugin. Proven by elimination, not by reading a name off the thing: BOTH vaults' local-rest-api `apiKey`s are rejected 401 by BOTH ports, while `<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/semantic-vault-mcp/data.json` records `httpPort` matching exactly. ✅ port↔vault mapping RESOLVED 2026-08-07 (was recorded unknown): the plugin config carries the port, so it was readable all along — the earlier probe looked in the local-rest-api config, which only ever records 27123/27124. ✅ REACHABLE from a Claude session since 2026-08-07 via the stdio bridge `wom7web/project/scripts/obsidian_mcp_bridge.py`, wired in the estate-root `.mcp.json`. The bridge exists because the server needs `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>` and CLAUDE.md forbids secrets in files: it reads the key at launch from the plugin's own gitignored `data.json`, so the credential is never copied into any config. It also reads the PORT from there rather than taking one on the command line — the two vaults have collided on ports before, and a hardcoded port would silently talk to the wrong vault. ⚠️ Session-ful transport: everything after `initialize` 400s unless the returned `Mcp-Session-Id` is echoed, and the server returns that header LOWER-CASED. 🔴 Exposes 8 tools incl. **`edit`**, and `readOnlyMode` is **false** in both vaults — an agent with these tools can WRITE to the vault. For `wom7web` that vault is a live code repo, so writes land outside the normal Edit/git path. ✅ **OWNER DECISION 2026-08-07: keep `readOnlyMode: false` on BOTH.** Write access is the point — the intended use is manual and Obsidian-tool analysis written back to `.md` through MCP. This is a deliberate, reasoned acceptance, not an unreviewed default. ⚠️ What that means in practice, and it is on the agent doing the writing: an MCP `edit` in the **wom7web** vault touches the code repo **outside** the Edit/git path, so it produces no diff you read first and can leave the working tree dirty without anything announcing it. 🔴 T186 (2026-08-08): this used to say *'prefer the wom7md vault for notes'* — **there is no second vault any more**, so that escape hatch is gone and every MCP write lands in a live code repo. `git status` afterwards is now the only check. Ties [[T144]]. Port 3007 → the **wom7web** vault, which is also the code repo.

_comment: T150 AC7 — WHICH SURFACE IS FOR WHOM, and why. Recorded as policy so the next agent does
not 'finish the MCP migration' by putting an unauthenticatable server in a hook.
agent_facing (MCP): interactive, agent-in-the-loop work. An MCP server may require an
OAuth flow, a browser round-trip, or a human approving a tool call. That is FINE here
because a human is present.
automation_facing (just/CLI): hooks, cron, CI, deploys — anything that runs with nobody
watching. These MUST be reachable with an injected secret and nothing else.
THE CONSTRAINT, stated plainly: MCP AUTH IS NOT HEADLESS. Several connectors authenticate
interactively and simply cannot complete in a non-interactive session — observed
2026-08-02, when `plugin:figma:figma` required an OAuth flow this session could not run.
A hook that depended on it would fail for a reason the hook cannot report and the operator
cannot fix from the error. That is why the mirror in .husky/pre-push calls `gh` directly
and not an MCP server, and why it is the single sanctioned forge call site (T150 AC3b,
enforced by hooks_check.py and proven RED by test_hooks_check.py).
A surface may be BOTH — codegraph has `codegraph_explore` (agent) and `just ask` (CLI).
That is the healthy shape: the automation path never depends on the interactive one.
boundary.rule: Automation MUST NOT depend on an MCP surface. If a hook, cron job or deploy needs a capability, it takes the CLI path — even when an MCP server offers the same capability more conveniently.

mcp._obsidian_note: Declared 2026-08-07 after `just mcp-exposure` surfaced three undeclared Obsidian listeners. Only the two MCP ports (3001, 3007) are declared here, per owner instruction. 🔴 The THIRD listener, 127.0.0.1:27123, is deliberately NOT declared as MCP: it is the plugin's REST half and it answers `GET /` with HTTP 200 while UNAUTHENTICATED, disclosing plugin id, version, Obsidian version and plugin directory. That is an information-disclosure surface, not an MCP server — it belongs in a security review, not in this list. ⚠️ Both open vaults' plugin configs declare the SAME ports (insecure 27123 / secure 27124), so only the first vault to start can bind them — a collision that makes which vault answers 27123 an accident of startup order. ⚠️ Both endpoints send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so any web page you visit may attempt cross-origin requests to them; the API key is the only barrier.

iac._comment: T125: infrastructure-as-code, declared so the gates can see it. THE RULE: `plan`/`drift` are read-only and safe to automate; `apply` is NEVER automated and never run by a gate. Terraform here can perform deployments via local-exec null_resources (TECH-DEBT D22), so an apply is not 'just infrastructure' — treat it as a deploy until that debt is paid.
iac.apply_policy: manual-only; requires a reviewed plan and no local-exec side effects
iac.owns: DNS/zone/ruleset config that wrangler does NOT manage. Workers custom domains are owned by wrangler — Terraform must not manage those records or the two fight.

backups._comment: T229 AC2 — how stale a backup may be before `just backup-freshness` calls it a missed run. In config because the CADENCE is a decision that changes more often than the checker, and a cadence written into a script is one nobody edits. ⚠️ These are AGE LIMITS, not a schedule: this estate's scheduler surface is split (desktop-app routines are invisible to the CLI scheduler), so freshness is verified by the artefact ON DISK, never by asking a scheduler. postgres=7 because the database changes constantly and 7 days is already a lot of lost work; storage=30 because it is append-mostly at ~54 MB a copy, so monthly is proportionate. Raise either only with a reason, and remember the storage copy proves completeness, not a restore.

supabase_limits._comment: T229 AC6 — OWNER DECISION 2026-08-18: stay on the Supabase FREE tier and do not hit the limits; Pro is available for the w0m project if genuinely needed, but Free is the default. A limit you have chosen to live inside must be watched, because these fail ABRUPTLY rather than gradually. versioning._comment: T131 AC1 — the w0m release version schema, declared ONCE so the gates can verify it. ROADMAP §4 requires YYYY.MM.DD-<unixtimestamp>; before this block it was applied in exactly one place and verified nowhere, which is how two orphaned producers survived in the tree. Verified by `just version-check` (project/scripts/version_doctor.py).

producer._comment: ONE producer. `just version` prints it; the justfile variable is the same expression evaluated once per invocation, which is what the deploy recipes interpolate. Any other site that constructs a version string is a second format waiting to happen — version-check finds them.
producer._consumers_comment: T131 AC6 — VERIFIED, not merely listed. `just version-check` now asserts each name here has a justfile recipe AND that the recipe interpolates `deploy_version`, so this list cannot claim coverage the justfile does not have. Its first run found `deploy-cfworkers` dangling: the recipe had been renamed `deploy-workers` (the 2026-08-01 worker-name split) and the declaration was never updated — invisible for as long as nothing checked. `build` joins the list because AC2 made it a real consumer; `_stamp` deliberately does NOT, because it takes the triple as arguments and never interpolates the producer itself.

scan._comment: WHICH SET version-check enumerates — stated, never implied. It scans tracked files under these globs in these repos. A version producer outside this set is invisible to the gate; widen the set rather than trusting a clean number (T149's standing rule).

exempt.package.json: T391: All governed private manifests (@wom root, wom7web monorepo, and apps/*) uniformly declare the canonical date-timestamp release version format. Because private: true is set across all apps, pnpm permits this without registry publishing friction. External published packages retain semver.
exempt.report filenames: Audit/report files use %Y%m%d_%H%M%S for UNIQUENESS, not release identity. ⚠️ This is a CATEGORY note, not a path — the matcher is path-substring, so it matches nothing on its own; the two scripts above are the concrete entries. Kept because the category is the reasoning future entries should follow.
exempt.project/scripts/w0m_audit.py: Report header prose (`%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC`) and the IDEMPOTENT per-day filename `W0M-STATUS-<day>.md`. Both fall under versioning.artifact_naming.does_not_apply_to — the header is written for a person, and the daily file's stable path is its purpose. Not drift: excluded by category, under the declared standard.
exempt.project/scripts/tools_check.py: A machine-parsed ISO `generated` field read back with datetime.fromisoformat to compute an age. Excluded by category under versioning.artifact_naming.does_not_apply_to: the release schema is not ISO-8601 and would not parse. It is a data field, not an artefact name.
exempt.project/scripts/tools_upgrade.py: T247 AC1 — the same category as tools_check.py above, and for the same field: a machine-parsed ISO `ran` timestamp in .tools-weekly-status.json, read back with datetime.fromisoformat to say how long ago the last toolchain run failed. It is a data field, not an artefact name or a release identity. ⚠️ This file DOES talk about versions constantly — it is the tool upgrader — which is exactly why the year+version heuristic fired here, and why the exemption is scoped to the timestamp rather than the file being waved through: any future release-shaped string in it should still be a finding.
exempt.project/scripts/tests/test_toolchain_cha: T247 AC7 — the regression proof for the toolchain chain. Its `datetime` use FABRICATES run timestamps (a 4-day-old failed run, a fresh clean one) to assert that a held tool is surfaced with its age, and its version strings are FIXTURES the checker is run against — the same category as wom7skills/tests/skills_version.test.ts. A test that must not contain version-shaped strings cannot test a version reconciler. ⚠️ Scoped to this file for that reason, not because test files are exempt as a class.
exempt.wom7skills/tests/skills_version.test.ts: T131 AC3's regression suite. The version strings in it are FIXTURES the checker is run against — a conforming one, a non-conforming `1.0` reproducing the pre-T131 state, and a deliberately varying producer that proves a no-op stamp stays a no-op even when the clock moves. None is a release identity and none reaches any artifact. ⚠️ Exempting a TEST is the narrow case: the thing under test is the version format itself, so it must be able to write bad versions on purpose. This does NOT extend to the tool it tests — `wom7skills/version.ts` is deliberately NOT exempt and is not flagged, because it reads `producer.expression` from this file rather than carrying a format of its own. If version.ts ever starts constructing a literal, the gate SHOULD fire on it.
exempt.wom7api/scripts/db_backup.py: T229 AC1 — the %Y%m%d_%H%M%S in `backup_<stamp>.sql` names a DUMP FILE for uniqueness and chronological sort; it is not a release identity and nothing reads it back as a version. Exempted by PATH rather than under the existing 'report filenames' category note because that entry says of itself that it is a category, not a path — leaning on it would make this exemption unverifiable. ⚠️ If this file ever produces a string that something PARSES as a version, this exemption is wrong and should be removed rather than widened.
exempt.wom7api/scripts/storage_backup.py: T229 AC4 — the %Y%m%d_%H%M%S in `storage_<stamp>/` names a BACKUP DIRECTORY for uniqueness and chronological sort, matching the `wom7api/scripts/db_backup.py` precedent exactly; nothing treats it as a release identity. ⚠️ Naming the caveat that precedent raises, because this case brushes it: `db_restore_verify.py` DOES parse `backup_<stamp>` back — but as the DUMP TIME used to tell post-dump growth from data loss, never as a version. A timestamp read as a timestamp is not the thing this gate exists to catch. If anything ever parses either stamp as a VERSION, both exemptions are wrong and should be removed rather than widened.
exempt.wom7web/scripts/hook_log_wrap.sh: T230 — the %Y%m%d_%H%M%S in `<repo>-<hook>-<stamp>.log` names a HOOK RUN LOG for uniqueness and chronological sort. Nothing parses it back as a version, and the file has no release semantics at all. Exempted by PATH, matching the `wom7api/scripts/db_backup.py` precedent where the date-stamp is likewise intrinsic to a generated filename. ⚠️ Distinct from `tasks_query.py`, which was REWORDED instead: there the word 'version' appeared incidentally in prose beside an unrelated date-parse, so removing it kept the gate's signal sharp. Exempt when the stamp is the file's job; reword when the match is an accident.
exempt.wom7api/scripts/backup_freshness.py: T229 AC2 / T231 AC4 — a FALSE POSITIVE with two halves, both stated because neither alone justifies the exemption. (1) The `%Y%m%d%H%M%S` is a strptime PARSE of `backup_<stamp>.sql` / `storage_<stamp>/` names, i.e. reading a date this file did not create — dating backup artefacts IS this file's job, matching the `db_backup.py` precedent. (2) The word that actually tripped the gate is `signature_version="s3v4"`, boto3's S3 CONFIG KEYWORD. \u26a0\ufe0f This estate's own rule is *exempt when the stamp is the file's job; REWORD when the match is an accident* — and the match here IS an accident, but it cannot be reworded: it is a third-party API parameter name, not our prose. That is the only reason this is an exemption rather than a rename. \ud83d\udd34 If a future version of this file constructs a version string, this exemption is wrong and should be removed rather than widened.
T155 — TWO non-release uses, both verified rather than waved through. (1) Line 73 `clientInfo: {name, version: "1.0"}` is the MCP INITIALIZE HANDSHAKE — the protocol's own field for a client identifying itself to the Upwork server. It is the version of this SYNC CLIENT as the remote sees it, not of any w0m release, and MCP fixes the field name. (2) Lines 439/447 `synced_at: %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` is an ISO timestamp recording WHEN a record was pulled, stored in the JSONL row. Neither is a release identifier; neither reconstructs the release expression. ⚠️ This file first tripped version-check on 2026-08-19 when `git add -A` swept it into an unrelated commit — the gate catching it there is why that mistake was noticed at all, so the exemption is narrowed to this PATH and not widened to the pattern.
exempt.wom7web/project/scripts/prepush_runner.p: T375 — ISO-8601 timestamps (datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()) recorded in checkpoint JSON to track step execution timestamps and durations. The word 'version' appears incidentally in the registered gate list citing the 'version-check' gate (T131). It is a diagnostic execution stamp, not a release identifier or artefact name.
exempt.wom7web/project/scripts/sync_manifest_ve: T391 — synchronizes governed workspace and sub-app package.json manifests with the canonical release version format emitted by `just version`. It propagates the declared producer's output; it does not define a competing release format.
exempt.wom7web/project/scripts/release.py: T481 — uses datetime.now() for persistent lock timestamps (~/.w0m/stable/.lock) and e2e test recording (~/.w0m/stable/e2e-result.json); release versions strictly come from declared producer (just version).
exempt.wom7web/project/scripts/db_drift_check.p: T551 AC4 — allocates and steps 14-digit numeric Supabase migration prefixes (`%Y%m%d%H%M%S`) for `supabase/migrations/<14digits>_<slug>.sql` (`just db-new-migration`). Supabase `schema_migrations.version` requires a purely numeric 8..14 digit prefix (`^\d{8,14}_`), not the release `YYYY.MM.DD-<unix>` format; this file allocates database migration sequence numbers, never release or artefact versions.

artifact_naming._comment: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14: the release format is ALSO the standard timestamp-versioned schema for generated ARTEFACT FILENAMES, not just releases. One schema, one producer, so an artefact can be lined up against a release without translating between formats. First adopter: deploy transcripts (`deploy-<version>.log`).
artifact_naming.producer: just version — NEVER reconstruct the expression at the call site
applies_to: generated artefact filenames that identify ONE run (deploy transcripts, export bundles, snapshot dumps)

does_not_apply_to._comment: A standard without a stated boundary gets applied where it does damage, or ignored wholesale once it does. These three are NOT timestamp-versioned artefacts and are excluded by category, with the reason each would break.
does_not_apply_to.machine-parsed timestamp FIELDS inside d: e.g. tools_check.py's `generated` ISO field, which is read back with datetime.fromisoformat to compute an age. The schema is not ISO-8601 and would not parse — this is a data field, not a name.
does_not_apply_to.human-readable time in report PROSE: e.g. w0m_audit.py's `%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC` header line. It is written to be read by a person, not matched by a gate.
does_not_apply_to.IDEMPOTENT per-day documents: e.g. docs/audit_and_research/W0M-STATUS-<day>.md. Its stable, predictable path is the point — a unix timestamp would mint a new file on every run and break every inbound link. ⚠️ Convert this one only alongside a decision about what links to it.

preflight._comment: T147 AC7 — the session-start preflight, declared here so a skill reads it instead of hardcoding a command. Answers 'is the environment wired up RIGHT NOW': MCP servers, graph index, repos, required binaries. Deliberately NOT a second toolset-status — that asks whether the governed registries are conformant and takes ~23s; this asks what a session can actually reach and takes ~1.6s, because AC1's whole point is that a preflight nobody runs is worse than none. 🔴 It REPORTS, it does not block (AC5): `skill check`, `discovery --enforce` and `state-check` already own the blocking, and a second blocking hook here would just be a slower push. ⚠️ It cannot tell you whether an MCP server is connected to the RUNNING SESSION — that is a harness fact, not a file or port fact, and both Obsidian servers were declared, enabled and listening for twelve days while zero Obsidian tools existed. It says so in its own output rather than printing a number it cannot measure.
preflight.session_hook: SessionStart in the estate-root .claude/settings.local.json, calling the script directly by absolute path rather than via `just`: the session's project dir is the estate root, which has no justfile, and `just` startup would cost ~0.5s of a 2s budget. Same single implementation either way.

skills_governance_scopes._comment: T147 AC2+AC4, owner decision 2026-08-17. TWO governance roots, not one. The project manifest (wom7web/.w0m/skills.json) governs .claude/skills; the USER manifest (~/.claude/.w0m/skills.json) governs ~/.claude/skills, which held 15 skills no manifest covered — real directories, no version, no integrity hash, loaded into EVERY session on this host while `check` printed '0 unmanaged' about the project tree beside them. They are governed separately rather than annexed by whichever project you happened to run from: a project manifest describes one repo, and these load everywhere. ⚠️ The user manifest is UNVERSIONED (~/.claude is not a git repo), so its decisions cannot be reviewed in a diff — accepted because the lockfile's job is DETECTION, which works unversioned; the reasoning belongs in a ticket. 🔴 Adoption is never automatic: `reconcile` with no decision flag only LISTS, and each skill is decided one at a time, because a bulk yes is indistinguishable from never having looked.

coverage_scan._comment: T147 AC3 — what is in the repos that NO stack claims. The INVERSE of `just discovery`, which is the whole point: discovery walks the REGISTRY and asks whether each declared thing is real, so it can only ever find what the registry already knows to look at — T149's organising finding verbatim ('a gate reports zero because it only looks where it already knows to look'). This walks the CODE and asks what nobody declared. 🔴 'Uncovered' means NO STACK DECLARES THE PATH — it does NOT mean ungated: pnpm-workspace.yaml globs `packages/*`, so `just typecheck` probably does reach packages/ui even though no stack entry names it. Both are true and they are different statements; registry coverage is the one that matters because the registry is what the gates read. Corpus is git-tracked (`git ls-files`), NOT the filesystem — the estate has already been bitten by that difference (a preflight globbed the disk and counted a gitignored file; .astro is 210 tracked vs 220 on disk).
coverage_scan.not_in_preflight_composite: Deliberately NOT added to preflight's FULL_CHILDREN. That table composes children by EXIT CODE, and this scan is report-only (always 0), so including it would print a green tick over a 524-item worklist — the exact vacuous-green shape T147 AC6 exists to prevent. It is also the wrong cadence: a worklist is something someone sits down with, not something a session start prints.

coverage_scan.exempt_key: `coverage_exempt` in stacks-policy.json maps <repo>/<path-prefix> to a REASON. Separate from that registry's `exempt` (which exempts a whole STACK from drift) because this exempts a PATH from needing a stack at all — a different decision about a different noun. Same T135 discipline: a reasonless exemption refuses.

deploy_logs._comment: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14: deploy transcripts rotate MONTHLY. They are gitignored working artefacts — one full deploy is ~170 KB, so an unrotated directory becomes the thing nobody opens. Rotation buckets by the month in the transcript's OWN NAME (the versioning.artifact_naming schema), not by mtime: a copied or restored file keeps its identity, and mtime does not.
deploy_logs.keep_months_reason: OWNER 2026-08-14: ONE month. A transcript's job is to explain the deploy you just did or the one that just broke — both are days old, not months. Older ones are reconstructable from the `deploy_log` table and the CHANGELOG, which are versioned; these are 170 KB gitignored working files. ⚠️ Pruning DELETES, and the recipe names every file it removes rather than reporting a count, because a silent delete and a no-op look identical.

tasks_surface._comment: T228 AC8 — TASKS.md is the traced queue and it had NO declared bound, while STATE.md has had one since T174. Measured 2026-08-20: 512,655 bytes, of which 231 ticket rows are 95%. The file does not grow by gaining rows — it grows by rows becoming essays: median row 1,420 B, longest 16,415 B, one row alone 3% of the file.

retention._comment: 🔑 These are TARGET numbers, not current ones. max_bytes is set BELOW today's size on purpose: a bound placed just above the present state declares the present state to be the norm, which is how the file reached half a megabyte unremarked. 409,600 is what remains once the 48 done rows (110,769 B, 21%) collapse — i.e. it is satisfied by doing AC8's rotation, not by editing the number.
retention._max_row_bytes: The binding constraint, and the one STATE.md's model has no equivalent for. A whole-file bound can be met while single rows keep swelling; 4,096 B is ~3x the median and leaves room for a genuinely dense row, while the current 16,415 B outlier is 4x it. ⚠️ A row over the bound is a REPORT, never an automatic edit — several long rows carry the only standing record of a live defect, which is exactly what T174's first rotation caught.
never_rotate: a `done` ticket that is still the SOLE record of something live — it needs a disposition row, not a move
any row whose gh_issue mapping would break — 223 issue links depend on it
